title: Dynamic Inventory Filtering
business: Small-scale e-commerce storefronts managing local product catalogs.
problem: High latency and poor user experience caused by full-page reloads for simple list filtering tasks.
solution: Alpine.js enables declarative, reactive UI updates directly within the HTML, allowing the browser to filter items instantly without server round-trips.
steps: Define the product list and search state within an x-data object.
Bind the search input to the state using x-model for two-way data synchronization.
Implement a getter function in x-data to compute the filtered list based on the current search input.
Use a template tag with x-for to iterate over the computed list and render the results dynamically.
outcome: A fluid, responsive interface where the product list updates in real-time as the user types.
limitation: Logic complexity is limited because all code resides in the HTML; as business logic grows, it becomes difficult to maintain and debug. Check for this by monitoring the size of the x-data object; if it exceeds 20 lines, consider moving logic to a separate JavaScript file.
